import math
from solution import distance_lat_long


def test_issue_example():
    """Issue example: distance_lat_long(23.5,67.5,25.5,69.5)==12179.372041317429."""
    result = distance_lat_long(23.5, 67.5, 25.5, 69.5)
    expected = 12179.372041317429  # issue literal for dlat=25.5-23.5=2, dlon=69.5-67.5=2
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_reversed_equals_example():
    """Paraphrases 'distance between two points': swapping endpoints keeps 12179.372041317429."""
    result = distance_lat_long(25.5, 69.5, 23.5, 67.5)
    expected = 12179.372041317429  # same issue literal, 23.5-25.5=-2, 67.5-69.5=-2
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_same_start_zero():
    """Paraphrases 'calculate distance': identical start point has distance 0."""
    result = distance_lat_long(23.5, 67.5, 23.5, 67.5)
    expected = 0  # 23.5-23.5=0, 67.5-67.5=0 so distance 0
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_same_end_zero():
    """Paraphrases 'calculate distance': identical end point has distance 0."""
    result = distance_lat_long(25.5, 69.5, 25.5, 69.5)
    expected = 0  # 25.5-25.5=0, 69.5-69.5=0 so distance 0
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_origin_zero():
    """Paraphrases 'calculate distance': origin to itself has distance 0."""
    result = distance_lat_long(0, 0, 0, 0)
    expected = 0  # 0-0=0, 0-0=0 so distance 0
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_negative_identical_zero():
    """Paraphrases 'calculate distance': identical negative coords have distance 0."""
    result = distance_lat_long(-23.5, -67.5, -23.5, -67.5)
    expected = 0  # -23.5-(-23.5)=0, -67.5-(-67.5)=0 so distance 0
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_distinct_positive():
    """Paraphrases 'distance': distinct points have distance > 0."""
    result = distance_lat_long(23.5, 67.5, 25.5, 69.5)
    bound = 0  # minimum distance 0; dlat=25.5-23.5=2 !=0 so must exceed 0
    assert result > bound


def test_issue_distinct_nonnegative():
    """Paraphrases 'distance': distance is never negative, so >= 0."""
    result = distance_lat_long(23.5, 67.5, 25.5, 69.5)
    bound = 0  # lower bound 0 for any distance
    assert result >= bound


def test_contract_callable():
    """Contract: solution.distance_lat_long is callable."""
    assert callable(distance_lat_long) is True  # True means callable


def test_contract_returns_number():
    """Contract: distance_lat_long returns a number."""
    result = distance_lat_long(23.5, 67.5, 25.5, 69.5)
    assert isinstance(result, (int, float)) is True  # True means type check passed


def test_contract_finite():
    """Contract: distance_lat_long returns a finite value."""
    result = distance_lat_long(23.5, 67.5, 25.5, 69.5)
    assert math.isfinite(result) is True  # True means finite, not inf/nan
